Suppose we have a dataset consisting of $4$ datapoints with $2$ features in the form of the $4 \cdot 2$ matrix
$X = \begin{bmatrix}0.40 & 0.21 \\ -1.49 & -1.44 \\ 0.42 & 0.85 \\ 0.67 & 0.38\end{bmatrix}$
where the data has been standardized (the mean of each feature is $0$ and the standard deviation is $1$).
We are also given the SVD decomposition $X = UΣV^{T}$ where:

$U|= \begin{bmatrix}-0.179 & -0.341 & 0.574 & -0.723 \\ 0.858 & 0.08 & 0.489 & 0.138 \\ -0.371 & 0.78 & 0.491 & 0.114 \\ -0.307 & -0.519 & 0.437 & 0.667\end{bmatrix}; Σ|= \begin{bmatrix}2.416 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.392 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}; V|= \begin{bmatrix}-0.708 & -0.706 \\ -0.706 & 0.708\end{bmatrix}$

Which of the following matrices corresponds to the one-dimensional version of the data that preserves the most variance?

1. $\begin{bmatrix}0.40 & 0.21 \\ -1.49 & -1.44 \\ 0.42 & 0.85 \\ 0.67 & 0.38\end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix}-0.708 \\ -0.706\end{bmatrix}$
2. $\begin{bmatrix}-0.179 \\ 0.858 \\ -0.371 \\ -0.307\end{bmatrix} \cdot 2.416$
3. $\begin{bmatrix}-0.708 \\ -0.706\end{bmatrix}$

Suppose we have a dataset consisting of $4$ datapoints with $2$ features in the form of the $4 \cdot 2$ matrix
$X = \begin{bmatrix}1.2 & 0.02 \\ -0.27 & 1.05 \\ -1.19 & -1.35 \\ 0.27 & 0.27\end{bmatrix}$
where the data has been standardized (the mean of each feature is $0$ and the standard deviation is $1$).
We are also given the SVD decomposition $X = UΣV^{T}$ where:

$U|= \begin{bmatrix}-0.411 & 0.663 & 0.61 & -0.141 \\ -0.262 & -0.743 & 0.606 & -0.113 \\ 0.854 & 0.091 & 0.501 & 0.105 \\ -0.182 & 0 & 0.104 & 0.978\end{bmatrix}; Σ|= \begin{bmatrix}2.102 & 0 \\ 0 & 1.257 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}; V|= \begin{bmatrix}-0.708 & 0.707 \\ -0.707 & -0.708\end{bmatrix}$

Which of the following matrices corresponds to the one-dimensional version of the data that preserves the most variance?

1. $\begin{bmatrix}-0.708 \\ -0.707\end{bmatrix}$
2. $\begin{bmatrix}-0.411 \\ 0.663 \\ 0.61 \\ -0.141\end{bmatrix} \cdot 2.102$
3. $\begin{bmatrix}-0.411 \\ -0.262 \\ 0.854 \\ -0.182\end{bmatrix} \cdot 2.102$

:knowledge-point/title: Identifying the Best One Dimensional Reduction Given SVD of Data
